symptom: ako/mxcli#2199: `show message information (if $Posted < 0 then 'a' else 'b');` passed `check --references` and `exec`, then mxbuild 11.16.0 reported CE0117 "Error(s) in expression." at Show message activity '{1}'.
cause: The writer was right. The type word belongs AFTER the message (`show message <expr> type Information`); written first, `information (…)` is a function call, so the message was the expression `information(if …)`, stored correctly as template '{1}' with that call as its parameter — and Mendix has no information(). MDL044 (unknown function) walks a fixed list of statement kinds in checkStmtExprFunctions; show message and validation feedback were not on it, so a call to any non-function in them passed check and exec.
file: `mdl/executor/validate_microflow.go` (checkStmtExprFunctions: ShowMessageStmt, ValidationFeedbackStmt; checkExprFunctions: message-type hint); `.claude/skills/mendix/write-nanoflows/SKILL.md` (seven type-first examples)
insight: `describe` of the written microflow answered it in one step: `with ({1} = information(if …))` shows the type word swallowed into the expression, which no BSON dump would make as obvious. The '{1}' caption looked like a template-encoding defect and pointed at the writer; the control that ruled it out was the parenthesised form `show message (if …) type Information`, stored the same '{1}' shape and built with the same errors as the control project. The likely source of the mistake is our own skill: write-nanoflows taught `SHOW MESSAGE WARNING '…'` seven times, each a parse error that only the parenthesised variant gets past. A per-statement list of expression sites (checkStmtExprFunctions) silently omits every statement nobody added — log was added for #1033, show message waited for #2199.
test: mdl/executor/validate_microflow_expr_test.go TestValidateMicroflow_UnknownFunction (type word written before show message, unknown in show message template param, unknown in validation feedback, + two accepted controls)
